correctness.rationale: For every integer d>=2, n>=1 and 0<=m<dn, (d/dz)^m(z^d-1)^n=z^r Q_m(z^d) with r=(-m mod d). Differentiation maps Q to rQ+dyQ' when r>0 and to dQ' when r=0, preserving positive roots (including their simple interiors) by Rolle interlacing of Q and y^(r/d)Q. The root z=1 multiplicity is exactly max(n-m,0), origin power r, and hence all complex zeros lie on d radial unit spokes. Hägg-Shapiro Theorem 1.4(i), an invoked external theorem, makes the limiting core connected and containing all d original roots; as it lies inside the star, connectedness forces every arm. This establishes shadow=core=star with no transient zeros. Independent direct SymPy differentiations/real root isolation for 140 (d,n,m) and exact z=1 multiplicities agreed; only the structural proof treats all d,n,m.
residual_risks: The global equality depends on the accurately scoped published connectedness theorem; if its definition of limiting core differed, the last step would require reconsideration.
